newsitem.title: UK: Spice Girls hit record with fourth number one.
newsitem.headline: Spice Girls hit record with fourth number one.

text.p: The Spice Girls were celebrating making pop music history on Monday after they became the first group to top the British charts with their first four singles.
The all-girl band shot straight to the number one spot with their new double A side, Mama/Who Do You Think You Are?. Profits from the hit will be donated to charity.

The Spice Girls -- Geri, Victoria, Mel B, Mel C and Emma -- have surpassed the achievements of Gerry and the Pacemakers, Frankie Goes to Hollywood, Jive Bunny and Robson And Jerome, who all hit number one with their first three singles
The group began their run of hits with debut single Wannabe and followed it up with Say You'll Be There and 2 Become 1.
Wannabe was number one in the United States, a feat which evaded even the Beatles with their debut single.
Geri, dubbed Sexy Spice, said she believed the friendship of the group would keep it together for many years.

"You never know what may happen in 10 years time. It could be I end up drifting into obscurity and collecting wood on a beach," she told a television interviewer. "But if all goes well it would be great if the Spice Girls were still together."
